item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Central School had a bottle collection. Children in each class brought empty bottles to school. The principal made a bar graph of the number of bottles from five classes.

[Image: Bar graph of number of bottles collected by five classes]

Which class collected 45 bottles?
item.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Bottles" marked from 0 to 100 with horizontal grid lines every 20 units (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). The horizontal axis shows five classes:
- "Miss Barber’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Mr. Chyn’s Class": bar reaches approximately 45 (just above 40, a quarter of the way to 60).
- "Mrs. Friedman’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Miss Gonzalez’s Class": bar reaches approximately 87.
- "Mr. Mack’s Class": bar reaches approximately 70 (halfway between 60 and 80).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Ahmed made a survey of the favorite color of the students in 4 classes.

[Image: Four bar graph figures labeled Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4 with 3 columns labeled Red, Green, and Blue on x-axis. Y-axis with values of 0 to 14 for Class 1 and Class 4 and values of 0 to 15 for Class 2 and Class 3.
• Class 1: Red value of 12, Green value of 10, Blue value of 8.
• Class 2: Red value of 10, Green value of 15, Blue value of 5.
• Class 3: Red value of 5, Green value of 10, Blue value of 15.
• Class 4: Red value of 7, Green value of 10, Blue value of 13.]

In which class do the fewest students choose blue?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four bar graphs arranged in a 2-by-2 grid, each showing student choices for favorite colors (Red, Green, Blue):
- Class 1 (top-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is shaded gray with a height of 12; Green is shaded black with a height of 10; Blue is unshaded (white) with a height of 8.
- Class 2 (top-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 10; Green is black with a height of 15; Blue is white with a height of 5.
- Class 3 (bottom-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 5; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 15.
- Class 4 (bottom-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 7; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 13.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

- Mon.: halfway between 20 and 30 (height 25)
- Tues.: level with 20
- Wed.: level with 30

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Class A and B each have 40 students.

[Image: Pie chart for Class A and bar graph for Class B]

There are more girls in Class A than in Class B. How many more?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two graphs representing student populations in Class A and Class B:
- On the left, a pie chart titled "Class A" showing a circle divided into two sectors. An unshaded sector representing one quarter of the circle (from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock) is labeled "Boys". The remaining three-quarters of the circle is shaded grey and labeled "Girls".
- On the right, a bar graph titled "Class B" with a vertical axis labeled with values from 0 to 24 in increments of 4 (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) with horizontal grid lines. The horizontal axis has two categories: "Boys", with a light-grey bar of height 24, and "Girls", with a dark bar of height 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Tally table of Favorite Ice Cream]

A teacher asked 30 students in her class the flavor of their favorite ice cream. The table above shows how the teacher recorded the students' responses.

In the bar graph below, which ice cream flavor corresponds to the bar that is labeled X?

[Image: Bar graph of Favorite Ice Cream]
reference_items.figure_description:
The item contains two visual elements:
1. A two-column table titled "Favorite Ice Cream" and "Number of Students":
   - Butterscotch: 4 single vertical tally marks (4)
   - Chocolate: 2 groups of 5 tally marks (10)
   - Strawberry: 1 group of 5 tally marks and 4 single vertical tally marks (9)
   - Vanilla: 1 group of 5 tally marks and 2 single vertical tally marks (7)
2. A vertical bar graph titled "Favorite Ice Cream":
   - The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Students" with grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10.
   - The horizontal axis is labeled "Ice Cream Flavor".
   - There are 4 shaded vertical bars from left to right:
     - First bar has height 10.
     - Second bar is labeled "X" below the horizontal axis and has height 9.
     - Third bar has height 7.
     - Fourth bar has height 4.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Mr. Johnson asked the students in his school about their favorite subject.

This pie chart shows how many students liked each of 5 subjects.

[Image: Pie chart titled Favorite Subject, divided into various sizes and labeled with Math about one-third, Science about one-fourth, History about one-fifth, Gym less than one-fifth, and Music less than one-eighth.]

Which graph shows the same information as the pie chart?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 25, History value of 20, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 15, History value of 15, Gym value of 15, Music value of 14.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 20, Science value of 25, History value of 30, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 25, Science value of 30, History value of 20, Gym value of 8, Music value of 12.]

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Favorite Subject" is divided into five sectors: Math (the largest sector, about one-third of the circle), Science (the second largest, about one-fourth of the circle), History (about one-fifth of the circle), Gym (smaller than History), and Music (the smallest sector, less than one-eighth of the circle). In order of sector size from largest to smallest: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.

Each of the four response options shows a vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Students" ranging from 0 to 35 with grid lines every 5 units, and the horizontal axis showing five subjects: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.
- Graph A: Math = 30, Science = 25, History = 20, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph B: Math = 30, Science = 15, History = 15, Gym = 15, Music = 14.
- Graph C: Math = 20, Science = 25, History = 30, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph D: Math = 25, Science = 30, History = 20, Gym = 8, Music = 16.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

Choose the value closest to it.
